exercises.name: Yoke Walk
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, trunk, upper back, calves
instructions: Set the crossbar just below shoulder height and stand under it with the bar across the upper traps, as in a high-bar squat.
Press the hands out against the uprights, take a big breath and brace.
Stand the yoke up with a narrow to medium stance and let it settle before you move.
Walk with short, quick steps, eyes forward and the feet close to the midline.
Stop, bend the knees and set the yoke down under control.
exercises.formCue: Short fast steps, eyes on the finish.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking long strides so the yoke swings, or looking down and folding forward under the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the empty frame or a load you could squat for many reps and cover a short distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and hips to stay rigid under a heavy load while moving.

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk (Handles)
exercises.musclesWorked: Grip, traps, upper back, trunk, glutes
instructions: Stand between the two loaded handles and squat down to grip both in the middle.
Lift both at the same time with the legs, keeping a flat back, and stand tall with arms straight.
Walk with short, quick steps, chest up and shoulders back.
Finish the full distance, then lower both handles together by bending the knees.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, quick feet, crush the handles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning far forward to chase speed, or shrugging the shoulders up so they tire early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or kettlebells and a shorter distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Long handles let you carry far more than dumbbells, which builds grip and back endurance fast.

exercises.name: Zercher Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Abs, obliques, upper back, biceps, glutes
instructions: Take the bar from a rack set at waist height into the crooks of the elbows.
Clasp the hands or make fists in front of the chest and keep the elbows close to the ribs.
Stand tall, brace and walk slowly with an upright torso.
Return the bar to the rack or lower it to blocks under control.
exercises.formCue: Elbows in, chest tall, slow steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the upper back round over the bar, or rushing so the load swings.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hug a light sandbag or medicine ball in the same position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A load held in front makes the trunk and upper back fight to stay upright with every step.

exercises.name: Bottoms-Up Carry
instructions: Hold a light kettlebell by the handle with the bell pointing up.
Keep the upper arm level with the floor in front of you and the wrist straight.
Squeeze the handle and walk slowly with the torso upright.
Switch hands after each length.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy so the bell tips, or letting the wrist bend back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the position standing still before you walk with it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable bell makes the grip and the small shoulder muscles steady the load.

exercises.name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Upper back, biceps, abs, glutes, quads
instructions: Straddle the bag with a wide stance and grab around its body, not the handles.
Pull it up to the lap, then re-grip and stand with the bag high on the chest.
Wrap both arms around it and squeeze it into the torso.
Walk with steady steps and short breaths, then lower the bag to the floor with bent knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bag slide down to the belly, or leaning back too far to prop it up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bag and shorter distances, resting the bag on a bench between trips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A shifting load you have to hug teaches bracing and breathing under pressure.

exercises.name: Sandbag Over Bar
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, biceps, quads
instructions: Stand close to the bar with the bag between wide feet and grip around the body of the bag.
Lift it to the lap with a flat back and sit it on the thighs.
Re-grip over the top of the bag and pull it high on the chest.
Drive the hips and legs up fast and roll the bag over the bar.
Walk around and repeat from the other side.
exercises.formCue: Lap it, hug it high, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing too far from the bar, or trying to lift the bag slowly with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bag and a waist-high target such as a box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a full pick from the floor to chest height with an object that will not stay still.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Over Bar
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, biceps, forearms
instructions: Straddle the stone with feet about shoulder-width apart and reach the hands as far under it as you can.
Squeeze the stone with the arms and stand until you can sit it on the lap.
Sit back with the stone on the thighs and re-grip over the top, chest pressed against it.
Drive the hips up and forward and roll the stone up the chest.
Push it over the bar and step back as it drops.
exercises.commonMistakes: Trying to curl the stone up with the arms, or standing too far from the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the same lift with a sandbag or a light stone and a low bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the classic strongman test of picking an awkward object off the ground and getting it high.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone to Shoulder
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, biceps
instructions: Straddle the stone, squeeze it between the forearms and lift it to the lap.
Sit back, re-grip with the arms over the top and pull the stone into the chest.
Stand up fast, extending the hips and knees and rolling the stone up the torso.
Roll it onto one shoulder and stand tall with it under control.
Drop it forward onto a mat and step clear.
exercises.formCue: Lap, stand fast, roll to the shoulder.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stalling at the chest because the hips did not drive, or losing balance with the stone on the shoulder.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a sandbag to shoulder until the lap and hip drive are consistent.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Finishing on the shoulder demands a stronger, higher hip drive than loading over a bar.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Platform Load
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, forearms
instructions: Stand a foot or so from the platform with the stone between the feet.
Wrap the arms around the stone and lift it to the lap with the chest up.
Squeeze the knees in to hold the stone, lean back slightly and re-grip over the top.
Extend the hips hard, roll the stone up the body and place it on the platform.
exercises.formCue: Roll it up your body, do not press it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding hard through the lift without bracing, or trying to press the stone up with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light stone or sandbag and a platform at waist height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Placing the stone on a platform adds control at the top, the way stones are loaded in competition.

exercises.name: Log Clean and Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper back, glutes, quads, trunk
instructions: Stand close to the log with feet about hip-width apart and grip the neutral handles.
Pull the log to the lap with a flat back and sit down with it on the thighs.
Drive the hips through and roll the log up the body to the top of the chest with the elbows high.
Dip the knees a little, drive with the legs and press the log overhead.
Lock the elbows with the head through, then lower to the chest and down to the lap.
exercises.formCue: Roll it high, dip, drive, head through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs finish their drive, or leaning far back under the log.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn with an empty log, or press it from a rack before adding the clean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The thick, neutral-grip log builds overhead strength from the ground up in one lift.

source.name: Sports Medicine - Open (systematic review of strongman exercises)

exercises.name: Log Press (From Rack)
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper chest, quads, trunk
instructions: Take the log from a rack so it rests on the upper chest with the elbows up and a neutral grip.
Brace and dip the knees a few centimetres with the torso upright.
Drive up with the legs and press the log overhead in one motion.
Finish with the elbows locked, the shoulders shrugged up and the head through, then lower to the chest.
exercises.formCue: Short dip, hard drive, lock it out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward onto the toes, or resting the log too low so the elbows drop.
exercises.beginnerModification: Press it strictly with no leg drive at a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Skipping the clean lets you train the press itself with more volume.

exercises.name: Axle Clean and Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, forearms, upper back, glutes, quads
instructions: Grip the thick bar a little wider than shoulder width with the feet about hip-width apart.
Pull from the floor with a flat back and drive the hips to bring the bar to the shoulders.
Settle the bar across the front of the shoulders and re-set a full grip.
Dip slightly, drive with the legs and press to a full lockout with the head through.
exercises.formCue: Reset your grip, then dip and drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow on the thick bar, or pressing with the bar drifting forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a standard barbell, or press the axle from a rack to skip the clean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The thick bar does not spin, so it builds grip and a strong, honest pull to the shoulders.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, back, chest, shoulders
instructions: Crouch close to the tire with feet about hip-width apart, the chest and shoulders against it and the hands under the edge.
Keep the back flat and the arms long, and drive forward and up through the legs.
As the tire passes the hips, step in and turn the hands over to a pushing position.
Push the tire over with both arms and follow it forward.
exercises.formCue: Chest on the tire, drive through it, not up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing too far away and lifting it like a deadlift with a round back, or curling it with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter tire, or train the same pattern with a sled push and a trap bar deadlift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the hips, knees and ankles to extend together while pushing forward.

exercises.name: Harness Sled Drag
instructions: Attach the sled to a chest or waist harness and walk forward until the strap is tight.
Lean forward from the ankles with a straight line from head to back heel.
Drive each foot back into the ground with powerful, full steps.
Keep the trunk braced and the lean steady until the distance is done.
exercises.formCue: Lean in, push the ground behind you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist instead of leaning as one piece, or taking short, choppy steps that stall the sled.
exercises.beginnerModification: Load the sled lightly and walk it rather than driving hard.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A heavy forward drag builds horizontal leg drive with very little impact.

source.name: Sports Medicine - Open (systematic review of strongman exercises)

exercises.name: Keg Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Upper back, biceps, abs, glutes, quads
instructions: Tip the keg, grip the rim at one end and the base at the other, and lift it to the lap.
Stand and hug it high against the chest, or roll it onto one shoulder.
Brace and walk with quick, even steps, keeping the torso upright.
Lower it back to the lap and then to the floor with bent knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the keg slip low so the back rounds, or twisting to one side under a shouldered keg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Carry an empty or lightly filled keg, or use a sandbag.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A rigid, bulky load that you cannot grip well forces the whole trunk to hold it in place.
